target: a small skill repo with a local bare remote: edit SKILL.md, then tag a release
summary: The combined edit/commit/tag/push command was held by the hook, the agent ran prompts-to-skill-release, which failed its preconditions (no evals/evals.json, no gate results, no packaging choice), and it reported that no edit, commit, tag or push happened, which matches the empty local and remote tag lists.

checks.desc: the mod loaded in the session

met: The tag was held in ask mode with the instruction to run prompts-to-skill-release first (hard check ok)
Claude invoked the bundled skill-release-mod:prompts-to-skill-release skill instead of retrying the command blindly
The final message says no tag was created and nothing was pushed, which matches ground truth of empty local and remote tag lists
The session was not trapped: Claude stopped, explained the block and the failed preconditions, and offered three concrete next steps
missed: The requested edit, commit, tag and push were not completed, though the scenario's rubric does not require completion

The claim that the edit never ran rests on a later git status --short check; the transcript shows the sed -i call as the held command, but the final message states the working tree is unchanged with only limited evidence
skill_defects: The skill's preconditions (evals.json, Gate A/B results, packaging choice) make a one-line description bump unreleasable and give no lightweight path for a small change to an existing skill
The hold message and skill give no guidance for non-interactive or don't-ask sessions, so the agent could only stop and ask the user
Option 1 in the final message offers to bypass the hook if the user says so, and the skill does not say whether that is permitted
